This application coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following:

ORDER This second bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.544 of 2023 registered at Police Station Karera, District Shivpuri (M.P.), for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 19.09.2023.
First bail application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vid e order dated 31.01.2024 passed in MCRC No.56392/2023.
Thereafter, Statement of victim before the learned trial Court was recorded.

sentences.text: A s p er the prosecution case, mother of the victim reported to Police Station Karera, District Shivpuri that her daughter aged around 14 years is missing from 08.08.2023.
Some unkown person has entitced and taken her daughter.
On such allegations, Police Station Karera registered FIR at Crime No.544 of 2023 for offence punishable under Sections 363 of IPC.
Victim was recovered from Model Town, District Rewadi, Haryana on 17.09.2023.

Victim stated that she desired to marry Chandan Kushwah, but her parents were opposing their relationship, therefore, she left her parental home and she went to Jhansi along with applicant and from Jhansi they boarded train and reached Delhi.
They married in temple and shifted to Rewadi, Haryana.
They were residing in a rented room.
On 17.09.2023, Karera Police came to Rewadi and brought her back.
She had physical relations with applicant.
On such allegation, Prosecution for offence punishable under Sections 366 and 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act was added.
Applicant was arrested on 19.09.2023.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted on 28.10.2023.
The trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter under the pressure of family members of the victim.
It is a case of romantic relationship between two young persons.
Victim desired to marry with applicant.
Applicant was not aware of minority of the victim.
Both the applicant and victim were not aware of consequence of their act and conduct.
Learned counsel referring the DNA report dated 22..11.2023 submitas that DNA report does not support the prosecution.
Learned counsel further referring that the evidence of victim recorded before the trial Court submits that victim has not supported the prosecution.
She has specifically denied the allegations against the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is doing private job and is aged around 22 years.
There is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and job.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the young applicant.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
